column1: # PRELIMINARY PARTIAL TABLE of the code of Grantham's despatches of 1778. A working aid, NOT a key. No printed or manuscript key was found.
# How made: fifteen despatches in SP 94/205 (2,314 code numbers) carry the office clerk's English between the lines, but not word over
#   number. Each despatch's numbers were aligned with its words in order by a script (scripts/build_table.py); a number takes the word it
#   keeps company with across despatches. No. 35 was not used.
# RELIABILITY (verifier's estimate, 15 Nov 2026): about two thirds of the 'firm' entries are right, so about one in three may be wrong.
#   Evidence: on despatches left out of the count, 70% of firm content-word entries and 82% of firm function-word entries fall in order in
#   the clerk's text, against 6.5% and 39.5% for tables with the words shuffled; on No. 35 itself 11 of 16 (shuffled: 3.6 on average).
#   Entries for common words (the, of, to, that, I ...) can match by accident because those words are everywhere; three firm entries are
#   already known not to fit No. 35 (717 'the', 423 'of', 1178 'should'). The reader's own estimate was 'about a quarter may be wrong'.
#   'weak' entries were aligned once, or not stably: treat each as a guess. Nulls and the numbers that spell names are not identified.
# confidence: firm = aligned to the same headword at least twice, in at least two thirds of its alignments, and stable across runs;
#             weak = anything less. headword: stem as the script keeps it (endings dropped: 'shoul' = should, 'noth' = nothing).
# forms: the clerk's words at the places aligned (a run of words means the number was matched to the last and the others had no number).
